evidence_excerpts: paradigm cases of grounding have the relevant epistemic feature, two of which we’ve already discussed: the grounding of [p∧q] in [p], [q], and the grounding of [p⁄q] in [p]
the connecting question, ‘Why should [p⁄q] obtain given that [p] obtains?’ certainly lacks cognitive significance
text: Paradigmatic grounding cases support the significance principle because their connecting questions lack substantive content even for minimally informed subjects.
